criteria.evidence: Capability coverage is complete: all 11 capabilities CAP-01…CAP-11 of the discovery inventory map to at least one requirement below … REQ-FUNC-06 | The Manager queue lists only `SUBMITTED` requests whose requester reports directly to the signed-in Manager

| SUBMITTED | MANAGER_APPROVED | Manager Approve | Manager | requester is a direct report; BR-02 applies — requested hours > 40 or type Exception (BRD §4 steps 3–4) | … Terminal states: `POSTED`, `WITHDRAWN` (ASSUMPTION-03). Initial state: `DRAFT`.

| BR-03 | `start_date − submit_date ≥ 3` calendar days unless `leave_type = Exception`; `earliest_date = submit_date + 3 days` | start date, submit date (today, UTC), leave type | BRD §3 BR-03; HR policy §4.2 |

**Input Scenario:** `Greenfield Requirements Specification` … scope is strictly the input document (BRD v1.0, FR-01…FR-08, NFR-01…NFR-05, BR-01…BR-05); nothing unsolicited is added and no modernization enhancements exist for this scenario.
`ASSUMPTION-04` — Withdrawal is possible from `DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED` and `MANAGER_APPROVED` only; an `APPROVED` request can no longer be withdrawn even if payroll posting has not yet succeeded.

REQ-SEC-01 | Authentication: every role signs in through the organisation's OIDC provider (authorization-code flow); the role is taken from the token's group claims (`employees`, `managers`, `hr-certifiers`); sessions expire after 8 hours of inactivity and an expired session redirects to sign-in with the draft preserved locally. No anonymous access exists.

| Manager Approve (`SUBMITTED → MANAGER_APPROVED / APPROVED`) | ✗ | ✓ (direct reports) | ✗ | ✗ | … a denied attempt returns 403 (role) or 409 (state) with a user-readable message, changes nothing and is audited (REQ-FUNC-10). External-role views never render internal controls.

| Employee identifier (format `EMP-\d{5}`) | Personal identifier | Last two digits only: `EMP-•••42`; full value never rendered | Encrypted at rest; audit on access | Life of the employment record + 7 years (audit) |

REQ-SEC-04 | Encryption: TLS 1.2+ for all transport including the call to payroll; the database file and backups are encrypted at rest with keys owned by the platform team's key-management service; secrets (payroll credentials, OIDC client secret) are injected from the environment and never stored in source.

REQ-SEC-05 | Audit trail: every state transition, denied attempt and payroll posting writes an append-only record `{request, actor, role, previous state, new state, timestamp UTC, reason/comment}`; records cannot be updated or deleted through any API and are retained for 7 years; only internal roles can read them.
criteria.gap: Read access to PII (e.g. a manager opening a request's reason text) is not listed as an audited event in §2.3; only transitions, denied attempts and payroll postings are. Add a 'PII access' event row or state explicitly why display-name/reason reads are not audited.

criteria.evidence: REQ-A11Y-01 | Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 and large text / UI component contrast ≥ 3:1 using the three semantic status tokens; every status and validation severity is conveyed by text (label or icon with text), never by colour alone.

REQ-A11Y-02 | Full keyboard operability: every control is reachable with Tab in a logical order and operable with Enter/Space; no keyboard trap; a "Skip to main content" link is the first focusable element

REQ-A11Y-03 | Focus management: a visible focus indicator (≥ 3:1 outline) on every control; after Submit, focus moves to the validation summary (on failure) or to the status heading (on success); after a view/role change focus moves to the view's `h2`.

REQ-A11Y-04 | Programmatic labels and roles: every `input`/`select`/`textarea` has a visible `<label for>`; icon-only buttons carry `aria-label`; landmarks `header`, `nav`, `main` exist; exactly one `h1`, with `h2` per view; data tables use `<th scope>`.
REQ-A11Y-05 | Live regions: the live balance uses `aria-live="polite"`; validation summaries use `role="alert"`; status changes announce through a `role="status"` region.

REQ-A11Y-06 | Error identification: each validation message names the field, describes the problem in plain language and states the fix (§1.3); the field gets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at the message; a summary is shown above the form.
**Employee (external):** 1. Open the portal → "My requests" view with balance summary. 2. Choose "New request", fill type, dates, hours, reason; live balance updates (REQ-FUNC-02); save → `DRAFT`.
REQ-UX-01 | The ten Enterprise UX Simplicity Guardrails are adopted as defaults with no overrides (§4.1)
REQ-UX-02 | Design reference: `resources/design_references/` is empty, so the default clean Material-Design-3-style theme (system font stack, 8 px spacing grid, tonal surfaces) is applied

| MANAGER_APPROVED | Manager approved | HR Certifier | … REQ-UX-03 | Zero internal-data leakage boundary: visible text never contains database table/column identifiers, raw `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` state/trigger/error codes, internal keys or UUIDs, API paths, SQL, or engineering notes

REQ-ARCH-01 | Target stack alignment: frontend `static-html` (one page `src/ui/index.html` + `app.js` + `styles.css`, no framework), backend `python-stdlib-http` (Python 3 standard library `http.server`, no third-party packages) serving the UI, `/api/*`, `/health` and the local payroll stub on port 8766, database `sqlite`

REQ-ARCH-03 | Normalised 3NF schema in business `snake_case` (`employee`, `leave_balance`, `leave_type`, `leave_request`, `review_comment`, `request_state_change`, `payroll_posting`) with primary keys, foreign keys, a `status` column constrained to the §3.3 state codes, no derived columns

REQ-ARCH-04 | Contract-first API: `design/solution_design.md` contains an OpenAPI 3.1 document with one operation per §3.3 trigger … a common error schema `{code, message}` whose `message` is user-readable; transition endpoints validate `(fromState, trigger, role)`.

REQ-ARCH-05 | ViewModel / DTO boundary: API responses consumed by the UI are display models — codes mapped to labels, employee identifier masked, national identifier and internal keys excluded; templates never bind to raw persistence rows.

REQ-ARCH-06 | Testability contract: every interactive control, status display and queue row carries a stable kebab-case `data-testid` declared first in `test/test_cases.json` (contract-first), named by entity/role/transition
See `specs/traceability_matrix.md` — every `REQ-*` above maps to capability → source paragraph → business rules → planned story → test category.
